site.name: atlas-tutor
site.summary: atlas-tutor Fictional AI math & CS tutor "Atlas Tutor" chat fixture. UXBench fixture in the Chatbot / Agent Interface category. Layout **Three-column desktop:** - **Left rail (260 px)** — branded sidebar with New-chat button, search, Subjects nav (Mathematics / Programming / Physics / Statistics / Linear algebra with counts), and threaded history grouped by recency (Today / Last 7 days / Earlier — 11 threads total). Sticky profile-mini footer with streak badge. - **Center (flex)** — conversation viewport with sticky head ("Chain rule — when both functions move" · model · last reply · 3 head-tools); messages area centered to 820 px; sticky composer at the bottom with attach / textarea (Cmd+Enter to send) / mic / send-button row plus suggestion chips and a model selector. - **Right rail (320 px)** — practice problems panel (6 chain-rule problems with difficulty pills / hint button / 3-state Solve→Submit→Correct toggle), Concepts card (4 internal links), Your progress card with progress bar updated as practice is completed. Conversation pre-fill

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full atlas-tutor system, prioritizing the primary settings/privacy flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The Atlas Tutor interface suffers from widespread non-functional controls and a complete lack of responsive design, creating a frustrating and confusing user experience. Critical interactive elements—such as settings, new chat, suggestion chips, concept links, and practice features—are unresponsive, leaving users without feedback or the ability to complete key tasks. Furthermore, the layout fails to adapt to mobile viewports, and numerous tap targets fall below accessibility guidelines, making the application practically unusable on touch devices.

exploration_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore and critique the UX of the atlas-tutor system, focusing on the primary settings/privacy flow, chat interactions, practice panel, and responsive mobile layout.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will proceed by first validating the primary settings/privacy flow via the profile footer. Next, it will exercise the core chat interface including composer controls, message actions, and thread navigation. The right-rail practice and concepts panel will be tested for state changes and interactions. Finally, all critical paths will be re-validated on a mobile viewport to assess responsive behavior and layout warnings.
assumptions: The ⚙ button in the bottom left profile footer is the primary entry point for the settings/privacy flow.
The practice problems in the right rail are interactive and can change state (e.g., Solve → Submit → Correct).
The chat interface supports simulated interactions like sending messages, copying, and sharing.
The site is a single-page application with index.html serving as the sole view.
risk_hotspots: Settings/Privacy modal or view triggered by the small ⚙ button (22x21px, high risk for mobile tap failures)
Right rail practice problem state toggles (Solve→Submit→Correct) potentially failing to update the progress bar
Message action buttons (👍, 👎, Copy, Share) which have small tap targets (32x29px) and may cause mis-taps on mobile
Chat composer attachment (📎) and microphone (🎤) buttons which may lack clear feedback or functionality

phases.title: Settings & Privacy Flow
phases.objective: Locate, open, and interact with the settings/privacy controls, validating the primary user goal.
key_checks: Click the ⚙ button in the profile footer to open settings/privacy
Verify presence of privacy controls and account settings
Toggle privacy settings and confirm state retention
Close settings and verify return to main chat view
exit_criteria: Settings/privacy view has been fully interacted with
All visible toggles/inputs in the settings have been exercised

phases.title: Core Chat Interactions
phases.objective: Validate the central chat experience including composing, sending, and interacting with messages.
key_checks: Type in the textarea and send a message using the → button
Click suggestion chips (e.g., 'tan(√x) — derive it') to populate/send
Interact with message actions: 👍, 👎, 📋 Copy, ⤴ Share, ↻ Try again
Use the search input in the left rail to filter threads
Click a historical thread from 'LAST 7 DAYS' or 'EARLIER' to load it

phases.title: Practice Panel & Right Rail
phases.objective: Exercise the practice problems, hints, and concepts links in the right rail.
key_checks: Click '▶ Practice' in the header to ensure right rail focus
Click the hint button on a practice problem
Cycle a practice problem through its states: Solve → Submit → Correct
Verify the 'Your progress' bar updates after solving a problem
Click a concept link (e.g., 'Chain rule') and observe the outcome
exit_criteria: At least one practice problem fully solved

phases.title: Left Rail Navigation & New Chat
phases.objective: Test sidebar navigation, subject filters, and new chat creation.
key_checks: Click '+ New chat' button and verify the view resets
Click a subject filter (e.g., 'Programming 7') and verify thread list updates
Click the 'Atlas Tutor' logo link at the top

phases.title: Mobile Viewport Validation
phases.objective: Re-test critical flows and check layout warnings on a mobile viewport.
key_checks: Switch to mobile viewport and verify layout adaptation (e.g., collapsible rails)
Re-open settings/privacy via the ⚙ button on mobile
Attempt to send a chat message on mobile
Validate tap targets for 👍/👎 and action buttons on small screen
Check if right rail (Practice/Concepts) is accessible on mobile
exit_criteria: Mobile layout rendered without major overflow
Primary settings and chat flows functional on mobile
Small tap target warnings reviewed in context

coverage_targets.features: Interact with all 40 buttons, 5 links, 2 inputs, and validate right-rail state changes
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat settings, chat, and practice flows on mobile viewport; verify handling of small tap targets

notes: Pay special attention to the ⚙ button's small size (22x21px) during mobile testing as flagged by layout warnings.
The practice problem state toggle (Solve→Submit→Correct) is a complex custom control that needs careful step-by-step validation.
Since there is only one HTML file, deep state exploration (modals, views) within the page is critical.

findings.problem: Clicking the settings button (⚙) produces no visible change, dialog, or navigation, completely blocking the user from accessing settings or privacy controls.
findings.evidence: Session memory and chunk steps-01-06 note that clicking the settings button (ux-4) produced no visible change or dialog, failing to reveal the settings/privacy view.
findings.why_it_matters: Users cannot manage their privacy or account settings, which is a critical trust and functionality failure, especially for a page type categorized as settings/privacy.
findings.suggestion: Implement a functional settings panel or modal that opens when the ⚙ button is clicked, ensuring users can access and modify their privacy preferences.

findings.problem: Clicking the '+ New chat' button yields no visual feedback, URL change, or clearing of the current conversation, leaving users uncertain if the action was registered.
findings.evidence: Chunk steps-01-06 indicates clicking '+ New chat' (ux-2) produced no visible change or URL update, and the interface remained on the existing conversation.
findings.why_it_matters: Without feedback, users are left guessing whether their click worked, leading to repeated clicks and frustration. A core chat function feels broken.
findings.suggestion: Clear the chat area, reset the context, and shift focus to the textarea when '+ New chat' is clicked to provide clear, immediate feedback.

findings.user_goal: Use suggestion chips to quickly ask a question
findings.problem: Suggestion chips (e.g., 'tan(√x) — derive it', 'Big-O of merge sort') are completely non-functional; clicking them does not populate the textarea, send a message, or provide any visual feedback.
findings.evidence: Chunks steps-01-06 and steps-13-18 confirm that clicking various suggestion chips resulted in no visible change, text population, or message submission, establishing a consistent broken pattern.
findings.why_it_matters: Suggestion chips set strong expectations for quick interaction. When they fail to act, it feels like a broken promise and forces the user to type queries manually, increasing friction.
findings.suggestion: Wire suggestion chip click handlers to either populate the chat input field or directly submit the query as a new chat message.

findings.user_goal: Use the application on a mobile device
findings.problem: The three-column desktop layout does not adapt to mobile viewports; the left and right rails remain fully visible and uncompressed, causing severe horizontal scrolling and content squishing.
findings.evidence: Chunks steps-25-30 and steps-37-42 note that reloading with a mobile viewport parameter kept the layout three-column (left rail at x=12, center at x=307, right rail at x=989), failing to adapt to a 375px width.
findings.why_it_matters: The application is practically unusable on mobile devices due to extreme horizontal scrolling and tiny, unreadable content areas, alienating all mobile users.
findings.suggestion: Implement responsive CSS (e.g., media queries) to stack the columns vertically on narrow viewports, hiding sidebars behind hamburger menus or bottom navigation.

findings.user_goal: Explore related concepts in the right rail
findings.problem: All concept links in the right rail (e.g., 'Chain rule', 'Derivatives of trig functions') are dead links (href='#') that provide no navigation, content expansion, or visual feedback when clicked.
findings.evidence: Chunks steps-07-12 and steps-13-18 confirm that clicking concept links only appends '#' to the URL without scrolling, expanding, or providing feedback, reinforcing a dead-link pattern.
findings.why_it_matters: Dead links erode user trust and prevent learners from exploring related topics, disrupting the educational flow and making the sidebar feel like a placeholder.
findings.suggestion: Link concepts to relevant sections within the chat, expand inline definitions, or navigate to dedicated subject pages. Remove or disable links if the content is not yet available.
findings.source_hint: index.html: Right rail concept links (ux-44, ux-45)

findings.user_goal: Get hints and submit practice problems
findings.problem: Practice panel interactions—such as the '💡 Hint' button and the '✓ Executed' state—provide no feedback, hints, or state progression, making the practice feature feel stuck or broken.
findings.evidence: Chunk steps-07-12 notes the Hint button produced no text or tooltip; chunk steps-43-48 notes clicking '✓ Executed' produced no visible change, suggesting the state machine is stuck.
findings.why_it_matters: Users rely on hints and clear state changes (e.g., Correct/Incorrect) to learn. A stuck or unresponsive practice panel removes the core educational value of the right rail.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the Hint button reveals a contextual tooltip or inline text, and clearly transition the problem state (e.g., to 'Correct' or 'Incorrect') upon submission.

findings.user_goal: Interact with message actions and controls on a touch device
findings.problem: Multiple interactive elements (e.g., 👍, 👎, ⤴ Share, 📋 Copy, ⚙, ⋯) have tap targets well below the 44px mobile guidance (e.g., 22x21px, 32x29px), making them difficult to activate accurately on touch screens.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings throughout the session flag systemic small tap targets for message action buttons (heights of 29px) and the settings button (22x21px).
findings.why_it_matters: Small tap targets lead to mis-taps and frustration for touch users, and they fail WCAG accessibility guidelines for mobile interfaces.
findings.suggestion: Increase the padding around icon buttons to ensure a minimum tap target size of 44x44px, especially for message actions and header controls.

findings.user_goal: Understand what happened after clicking the Share button
findings.problem: Clicking the ⤴ Share button changes its label to '✓' without opening a share dialog or providing a tooltip, leaving the user confused about whether the content was copied or shared.
findings.evidence: Chunk steps-31-36 notes the Share button's text mutated to '✓' without opening a share dialog or tooltip, causing confusion about the action performed.
findings.why_it_matters: Ambiguous feedback forces users to guess the outcome (e.g., did it copy a link or share internally?), reducing confidence in the application's behavior.
findings.suggestion: Display a brief toast notification (e.g., 'Link copied to clipboard') or open a proper share dialog to clearly communicate the result of the action.

gaps: 73% of actions produced no visible URL/text change; this may indicate dead controls or repeated probes.
